prior_year_events.event_name: Adverse claims development from old case file review and US court rulings
prior_year_events.impact_description: Syndicate was required to strengthen reserves primarily in its Professional Indemnity, Financial Institutions, Miscellaneous and Management & Transactional Liability classes due to an extensive review of old case files by the newly strengthened team of in-house claims experts, and a series of unexpected adverse US court rulings, which contributed a further $53m of losses.

data.standardized_narrative: Antares Syndicate 1274 experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of $130.209 million in 2020, representing 12.9% of its opening gross reserves. This adverse development was primarily driven by an extensive review of old case files by a strengthened claims team and unexpected adverse US court rulings, particularly impacting Professional Indemnity, Financial Institutions, Miscellaneous, and Management & Transactional Liability classes, contributing $53 million to losses. The deterioration also included recalibration of IBNR. The year also saw a $29 million impact from COVID-19 and effects from US hurricanes Laura and Delta.

The deterioration comprises net claims including the change in claims incurred but not reported ('IBNR')
data.data_quality_notes: The narrative on page 9 explicitly states a NET prior year deterioration of $53.039 million. However, as per instructions, the GROSS prior year development of $130.209 million was calculated from the Gross Claims Development Table on page 12, by summing the changes in estimates for underwriting years 2011-2018. The $53 million mentioned in the narrative is a contributing factor to the overall strengthening, not the total gross prior year development. Lob movements are not quantified individually in the report for the total prior year development.
